# Intenter

> Intenter is a local, deterministic permission layer for AI coding agents that approves what a command actually does, not the string it was typed as.

- Intenter sits between an AI coding agent and the shell. It resolves each command to its real effects — following `npm run`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, Gradle and Maven wrappers to the script they actually execute — classifies every path it touches, and decides from that rather than from the command text.
- Decisions are deterministic and local. There is no language model in the decision path, no telemetry, no account and no network call in a decision: the same resolved command always gets the same answer, offline. The only outbound request the binary makes is an optional, anonymous check of the public release page for a newer version, which `INTENTER_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` switches off.
- An approval records the resolved effects plus a fingerprint of every mutable input the resolution depended on — the script, the lockfile, the build configuration. Change one and the approval stops matching, and the agent is asked again with an explanation of exactly what changed. A string rule such as `Bash(npm run *)` keeps matching after the script is edited; an Intenter approval does not.
- A small set of catastrophic actions is blocked no matter what was approved: deleting your home directory, writing to system locations, reading credential files, force-pushing to a protected branch, piping a download into a shell.
- It works with Claude Code on macOS, Linux and Windows, gating Claude's `Bash` and `PowerShell` tools. Install with `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vadym903/Intenter/main/install.sh | sh` on macOS and Linux, or `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vadym903/Intenter/main/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows, then run `intenter setup claude`.
- It is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0: free for personal and other noncommercial use; selling it or using it commercially requires a separate license. It is not open-source software in the OSI sense.
- What it is not: not a sandbox — a command it allows runs with your privileges; not a replacement for Claude Code's own permission system, which it adds to and never overrides; not a scanner of the files an agent edits directly, only of the shell commands it runs.
